clue.text: Giving sauce, often gets cut

definitions.meaning: the pickled flower bud of a shrub, which flavours a classic sauce served with mutton
a frolicsome leap, the thing one 'cuts' in the idiom 'cut a ...'

explanation.surface: A cook complains that whatever gives the sauce its flavour usually ends up chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' suggests chopping in the kitchen, but the second sense is the idiom 'to cut a caper', to leap about playfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: the edible bud used in sauce, and the playful skip people are said to cut.

clue.text: Close decision

definitions.meaning: the end or finish of something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the ending of something and a settled judgement arrived at.

clue.text: Nice to look at? Rather!

definitions.meaning: fairly or quite, as an adverb

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as an adjective for attractive and as an adverb meaning fairly or somewhat.

clue.text: Again, got bad pleaders confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the word next to it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Mixed-up lawyers have made a case go wrong all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall back into illness or bad habits after improving is to go bad again.

clue.text: Won't say what he feels is an odious fellow

definitions.text: Won't say what he feels is an odious fellow

parts.words: Won't say what he feels is an odious fellow
parts.note: a man who hides his true feelings and pretends otherwise is a two-faced, contemptible sort

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps his feelings to himself is being called a nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissembler who professes feelings he does not hold is a classic object of contempt.

clue.text: Doesn't move off the ground

parts.note: read as staying in one place while off the ground, as a kestrel or helicopter does in the air

explanation.surface: Something stays rooted to the spot and never budges.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as staying grounded; the cryptic reading puts 'off the ground' with the subject, which stays still in mid-air.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay suspended in one place in the air is to remain unmoving while off the ground.

clue.text: Crowd round Spanish river to see holy lady

indicators.note: round means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: to crowd someone is to press them
Rio is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: A crowd gathers by a river in Spain hoping to glimpse a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a nunnery, or deputy to an abbess, is a religious woman of rank.

clue.text: Metal used to keep the peace, commonly

definitions.text: used to keep the peace, commonly
definitions.meaning: a colloquial word for a police officer

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a reddish metal and, in slang, a policeman who keeps order.

clue.text: Open pointed tin cans, for example

indicators.note: opening the cans lets their letters spill out to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E for east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Someone prises open some sharp-edged tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' rearranges E (east, the point) with TINCANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an instance is to cite a single case as an illustration.

clue.text: Devilish part is wicked indeed

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Being devilish is certainly a wicked trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked is morally bad, sinful.

clue.text: Small house physicians here

parts.note: a little country building where doctors work, read as a modest village institution

explanation.surface: Doctors practise in a tiny dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural infirmary staffed by local doctors was the traditional village medical centre.

clue.text: Novel old Greek

definitions.meaning: the Latin name of the hero Odysseus

explanation.definitionFit: Joyce's novel takes its title from the Latin form of Odysseus, the Homeric wanderer.

clue.text: Run these little trips for someone else

definitions.text: Run these little trips for someone else

parts.words: Run these little trips for someone else
parts.note: short outings made to fetch or deliver something on another's behalf, which one is said to run

explanation.surface: A helper makes short jaunts at someone else's request.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tasks done for another person, typically shopping or delivering, are what one runs.

clue.text: Phrase reads: "new king left out parts of old weapons"

indicators.note: new means the letters are rearranged into a fresh order
left out means a letter is dropped from the pool before rearranging

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a phrase about missing a king from ancient weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of PHRASE READS, leave out R (king, from 'left out'), and 'new' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed metal tips of lances were the business ends of old weapons.

clue.text: Performed warlike act abroad? Certainly couldn't at home!

definitions.text: Performed warlike act abroad? Certainly couldn't at home!

parts.words: Performed warlike act abroad? Certainly couldn't at home!
parts.note: an army entering foreign territory by force, something no one can do to their own country

explanation.surface: Someone did something hostile overseas but would never dare at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Entering another country by force is a warlike act that can only happen beyond one's own borders.

clue.text: The opposite of flat, as it were

definitions.text: The opposite of flat, as it were

parts.words: The opposite of flat, as it were
parts.note: flat suggests horizontal, and its opposite is upright

explanation.surface: Something is the reverse of flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' might suggest sharp or lively, but here it means level, so the opposite is upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright, at right angles to the horizon, contrasts with lying level.

clue.text: Master one following him

parts.note: a follower of a teacher or master

explanation.surface: Someone trails behind a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower who learns from and adheres to a teacher's doctrine.

clue.text: Great, to be this? Absolutely!

parts.note: being great absolutely, without limit, means being highest of all

explanation.surface: Would it be great to be this? Yes, completely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely!' reads as eager agreement but cryptically qualifies 'great': great in the absolute sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest in rank or degree, great beyond comparison.

clue.text: Feel a cup shattering — though it's quite undisturbed

indicators.note: shattering breaks the words into pieces that are reassembled

explanation.surface: Feeling a teacup break, yet staying perfectly calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and tranquil, free from disturbance.

clue.text: Thoroughly mastered English — but they didn't speak it

definitions.text: Thoroughly mastered English — but they didn't speak it

parts.words: Thoroughly mastered English — but they didn't speak it
parts.note: the 1066 conquerors subdued the English people while speaking French

explanation.surface: Someone learnt English perfectly yet never spoke it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mastered English' looks like learning the language; it means conquering the English people in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-speaking invaders from northern France conquered England in 1066.

clue.text: Deed means a court case

explanation.definitionFit: The word means something done and also a legal proceeding brought in court.

clue.text: Loudly rattle — oddly, an obsequious thing to do

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: oddly signals the following word is rearranged in a strange way

explanation.surface: Rattling something noisily and strangely is a fawning gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise someone excessively to win favour is sycophantic behaviour.

clue.text: Is taken from his gifts; violent struggles result!

indicators.note: result signals the remaining letters form something new once rearranged
taken from means letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Someone's presents are confiscated, and brawls follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and S from HISGIFTS ('taken from') and rearrange the rest ('result').
explanation.definitionFit: Brawls and battles are violent struggles.

clue.text: Bird has a piece, and a tasty one

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: A bird has a morsel, and a delicious one too.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dainty morsel of food, a tasty piece.

clue.text: Just the thing to provide music at a tea-party?

definitions.text: Just the thing to provide music at a tea-party?

parts.words: Just the thing to provide music at a tea-party?
parts.note: the item that boils water for tea and sings a shrill tune when ready

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the ideal entertainment for a tea-party.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle fitted with a whistle sounds a note as it boils, playful music for tea.

clue.text: Shakes funny fellows

definitions.meaning: moves to and fro, as a dog's tail does

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to waggle from side to side and also humorous jokers.

clue.text: Sharp little bits, on the whole? No, off it

definitions.text: Sharp little bits, on the whole? No, off it

parts.words: Sharp little bits, on the whole? No, off it
parts.note: sharp slivers broken off a larger piece of wood or glass

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is sharp bits overall, the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the whole' looks like 'in general', but these bits are literally off the whole, broken from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin sharp fragments that have broken away from a larger piece.

clue.text: Wind instruments don't start to be stringed ones!

indicators.note: don't start means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: flutes are woodwind instruments

explanation.surface: Wind instruments that don't begin playing become string instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucked instruments with a rounded body, examples of stringed instruments.
